name: jobboard
description: Running and finished jobs from the jobrun registry: progress, rate, ETA, logs, stop.

commands.title: Job Board: Set Up jobrun for Terminal and Agents

jobboard.finishedDays.markdownDescription: Show finished jobs of the last N days. Nothing is deleted; see `#jobboard.autoCleanDays#` for that.

enumDescriptions: A job or group finished successfully.
A job failed (non-zero exit, signal, time limit, out of memory) or its supervisor vanished (lost).
A job was stopped while running.
A waiting job was cancelled, e.g. because a dependency failed.
A running job has made no progress for far longer than usual (see Stall Factor).
A job reported a problem with a `JOBRUN_EVENT error|warn <message>` log line.
jobrun cut the middle out of a job's log (see Max Log MB), or a log it does not write grew past that size.

jobboard.notifyOn.markdownDescription: Show a notification for these events while a VS Code window is open.

enumDescriptions: ETA in 2h10m
ETA 16:40 (in 2h10m)
jobboard.etaFormat.description: How the expected end time is shown.

enumDescriptions: Steps per second, minute or hour.
Expected end time.
Time since the last step, next to the average step time (⚠ when stalled).
Running time.

jobboard.rowDetails.description: What a running job's row shows after its progress. Hidden parts stay in the tooltip; a stalled job always shows its last step.

enumDescriptions: Running and Finished sections.
One section per machine or Slurm node, running jobs first.
One list, running jobs first.
jobboard.groupBy.description: How the job list is organized.

enumDescriptions: Count running jobs.
Count running, starting and waiting jobs.
No status bar item.
jobboard.statusBar.description: The job count in the status bar.

jobboard.diskWarnGB.description: Warn at the top of the job list when the disk with the registry or a running job's log has less than this many GB free (0: never).

jobboard.stallFactor.markdownDescription: A running job counts as stalled (⚠) after this many average step times without progress, also more than `#jobboard.stallGapFactor#` times the longest recent gap between steps, and at least `#jobboard.stallMinSeconds#`. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.stallGapFactor.description: A job counts as stalled only after this many times the longest gap between its recent steps without progress, so jobs whose steps arrive in bursts (parallel workers) are not flagged during their usual pauses. 0: ignore gaps. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.stallMinSeconds.description: A job counts as stalled only after at least this many seconds without progress. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.maxLogMB.markdownDescription: Cap for the logs jobrun writes (`jobrun run`). Beyond it jobrun cuts the middle of the log, keeping its start (`#jobboard.logKeepHeadMB#`) and its newest half of this size; the job is not affected. 0: no cap. Logs of Slurm and adopted jobs are only reported. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.logKeepHeadMB.markdownDescription: Start of a capped log that is always kept (configuration, early warnings); at most a quarter of `#jobboard.maxLogMB#`. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.autoCleanDays.markdownDescription: **Delete** finished jobs that ended more than this many days ago, with the logs jobrun wrote (logs it only read are kept). Checked at most once an hour. 0: never. Should be longer than `#jobboard.finishedDays#`. Stored in the registry's config.json (`jobrun config`), so it applies on every machine that uses the registry, also without VS Code; a JOBRUN_* environment variable takes precedence.

jobboard.command.description: Path to the jobrun CLI. Empty: ~/.local/bin/jobrun if present, else jobrun on PATH.

jobboard.registry.description: Registry directory (JOBRUN_HOME). Empty: the CLI default ~/.jobs.

jobboard.refreshSeconds.description: Refresh the job list every N seconds while it is visible.

jobboard.notifyOnFinish.description: Show a notification when a job finishes while this window is open.

jobboard.updateWhileUnfocused.description: Keep redrawing the job list while VS Code is not focused (e.g. watched on a second monitor). Off: the list is redrawn once when the window regains focus; status bar and notifications stay live.

jobboard.resourceSeconds.description: Measure CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM every N seconds while the Resources view is visible; values are means over this interval.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No jobs yet. Start a few short example jobs to see progress, stages and dependencies:
[Run Demo Jobs](command:jobboard.demo)
Use `jobrun` in your terminal and let your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) register their jobs:
[Set Up Terminal and Agents](command:jobboard.setup)
Then start jobs with `jobrun run --name NAME -- COMMAND`. [Documentation](https://github.com/KreitnerL/jobboard#readme)
